title: Hydrocarbons
content: Hydrocarbons are the compounds that contain only carbon and hydrogen.
e: Hydrocarbons are the compounds that contain only carbon and hydrogen. Hydrocarbons contain only carbon and hydrogen, joined by covalent bonds. Organic chemistry is built on carbon-hydrogen frameworks with covalent bonds.

title: Saturated hydrocarbons
content: Saturated hydrocarbons are hydrocarbons that contain only single bonds between carbon atoms.
e: Saturated hydrocarbons are hydrocarbons that contain only single bonds between carbon atoms. Hydrocarbons with only carbon-carbon single bonds are saturated. Hydrocarbons contain only carbon and hydrogen, joined by covalent bonds.

title: Unsaturated hydrocarbons
content: Unsaturated hydrocarbons are hydrocarbons that contain double or triple covalent bonds between adjacent carbon atoms.
e: Unsaturated hydrocarbons are hydrocarbons that contain double or triple covalent bonds between adjacent carbon atoms. Unsaturated hydrocarbons have a carbon-carbon double or triple bond, so alkenes, alkynes and aromatics sit in that group. Hydrocarbons contain only carbon and hydrogen, joined by covalent bonds. Saturated hydrocarbons contain only single bonds between carbon atoms.

title: Alkanes
content: Alkanes are hydrocarbons that contain only single bonds.
e: Alkanes are hydrocarbons that contain only single bonds. Hydrocarbons with only carbon-carbon single bonds are saturated. Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons with only single bonds and the general formula CnH2n+2. Hydrocarbons contain only carbon and hydrogen, joined by covalent bonds.

title: Alkenes
content: Alkenes are unsaturated hydrocarbons that contain a carbon-carbon double bond.
e: Alkenes are unsaturated hydrocarbons that contain a carbon-carbon double bond. Unsaturated hydrocarbons have a carbon-carbon double or triple bond, so alkenes, alkynes and aromatics sit in that group. Alkenes are unsaturated hydrocarbons with a carbon-carbon double bond and the general formula CnH2n. Hydrocarbons contain only carbon and hydrogen, joined by covalent bonds.

title: Alkynes
content: Alkynes are unsaturated hydrocarbons that contain a carbon-carbon triple bond.
e: Alkynes are unsaturated hydrocarbons that contain a carbon-carbon triple bond. Unsaturated hydrocarbons have a carbon-carbon double or triple bond, so alkenes, alkynes and aromatics sit in that group. Alkynes are unsaturated hydrocarbons with a carbon-carbon triple bond and the general formula CnH2n-2. Hydrocarbons contain only carbon and hydrogen, joined by covalent bonds.

title: Functional Group
content: A functional group is a group of atoms that represents a potential reaction site in an organic compound.
e: A functional group is a group of atoms that represents a potential reaction site in an organic compound. An organic compound has carbon and hydrogen with at least one C-C or C-H covalent bond. A functional group is the atom or group that sets the characteristic reactions of an organic molecule.

title: Isomers
content: Isomers are two or more compounds with the same molecular formula but different arrangements of atoms and have different properties.
e: Isomers are two or more compounds with the same molecular formula but different arrangements of atoms and have different properties. Isomers share a molecular formula but differ in how the atoms are arranged, so their properties differ. The molecular formula gives the actual number of each kind of atom in one molecule.

title: Hydrogenation
content: Hydrogenation is the reaction in which adding pairs of hydrogen atoms to a double or triple bond.
e: Hydrogenation is the reaction in which adding pairs of hydrogen atoms to a double or triple bond. Hydrogenation adds hydrogen across a double or triple bond and saturates the molecule.

title: Substitution Reaction
content: Substitution reaction is a reaction in which an atom or a group of atoms attached to a carbon atom is replaced by another atom or group of atoms.
e: Substitution reaction is a reaction in which an atom or a group of atoms attached to a carbon atom is replaced by another atom or group of atoms. In a substitution reaction one atom or group on carbon is replaced by another.

title: Dehydration Reaction
content: Dehydration reaction is the reaction in which H and OH are eliminated from adjacent carbon atoms to form water and a more unsaturated bond.
e: Dehydration reaction is the reaction in which H and OH are eliminated from adjacent carbon atoms to form water and a more unsaturated bond. Unsaturated hydrocarbons have a carbon-carbon double or triple bond, so alkenes, alkynes and aromatics sit in that group. Dehydration of an alcohol removes H and OH from adjacent carbons to make an alkene and water.

title: Fermentation
content: Fermentation is a process in which ethanol is made from glucose using yeast in the absence of air.
e: Fermentation is a process in which ethanol is made from glucose using yeast in the absence of air. Fermentation uses yeast without air to turn glucose into ethanol and carbon dioxide.
